en: So this is the ruin that\nreproduces memories. Truly\nfascinating.
Hmm? What is that glowing\nthing over there?
Uncle Ernest, wait up~! I want\nto see it too!
Hmm, was it Relia? To take an\ninterest in ruins at your age\nshows promise. Not bad at all.

However, fieldwork is vital for
an archaeologist. You had
better build up your physical
strength.
Okay, I got it. I'll do my best!

Miss Lilia, if I may, I would
suggest that there is no need
to decide your future dreams
at such a young age.

So many possibilities lie ahead
of you while you are still young.
It won't be too late to decide
on your future after you have
seen them.
Uh... so... um, does that mean I\nshouldn't build up my\nstrength?
Okay, I got it! I'll try all sorts of\nthings!
I-I am sorry, Captain. I intended\nto offer advice, but it seems I\nhave only confused Miss Lilia.

So that light from earlier was
coming from this ore... I'll try a
component analysis with the
Quad Scanner.
It's so clear and beautiful...\nJust like the blue sky over\nSthal Village.
Oh, look! There's another stone\njust like it over there.
Eh!
Why are the clouds white and\nthe sky blue?
Um, well, that's...
Why is the soil soft, but the\nstones are hard? Hey, why?
Fidel and me...? And this place,\nit's Sthal Village, right?
It's just as I heard. An image\nprojection using unknown\ntechnology, not a hologram.
Relia, is this sight part of your\nmemories?
Yeah. I remember asking Fidel\nall sorts of questions like this.
But...
...You know, back then, I did\nsomething bad to Fidel.

I thought Fidel knew
everything, so I just kept
asking him "why, why" about
everything I was curious
about...

Relia, why are you so
downcast? Having questions is
a good thing. It creates
opportunities for new learning.
But it troubled Fidel.

That is also a good thing. Being
troubled means that, at that
time, Fidel took the blue sky
for granted and hadn't even
questioned it.

As one grows older, it becomes
easier to overlook questions
regarding the things one sees
every day.
You could say that by posing\nthose questions, you gave Fidel\nan opportunity to learn as well.

...Actually, not long after Fidel
started studying on Earth, he
came to explain to me why the
sky is blue.

I thought he went out of his
way to look it up because I had
asked him so many things back
then.

Remembering such a mundane
conversation suggests he was
also curious about why the sky
is blue.
It seems Miss Lilia's questions\nserved to stimulate his\nintellectual curiosity.
Was I... able to be of help to\nFidel?
Yes, without a doubt.
Then, I'll keep asking you things\nwhenever I don't understand!
No, you mustn't do nothing but\nask questions, Miss Lilia.
Eh?

When in doubt, do not neglect
the effort to think for yourself,
form hypotheses, and find your
own answers.
Hmm!?

Hmm, no matter how many
times I see it, it's so strange...
How can we shop when there's
nobody here?
By "shop," do you mean this\nvending machine?
That's it! When E-tan puts\nmoney in here, all sorts of\nthings come popping out...

Is this inside the Cardianon...?
These are memories from
shortly after meeting Mista
Edge and the others.

Oh, I know that! It's a vending
machine, right? I saw them on
Earth. You put money in, and
all kinds of things come out.
Miss Lilia, it seems you have\nfully adjusted to life on Earth.
Now then, Miss Lilia. Do you\nhappen to know how a vending\nmachine works?

Um... You put money into the
machine, and then the product
you chose is replicated and
comes out.
Then, next is the mechanism of\nreplication. How do you think\nthe replication process works?
Hmm... Why?

Simply asking questions will not
lead to your own learning. You
must form a hypothesis
through logical thinking.
Logi-cal... thinking?

Don't overcomplicate it. Just
use your experience and
knowledge to imagine, step by
step, how it could be achieved.
Um...

I'm telling you, there's someone
inside! Or maybe they're using
Curse Crests to summon
them?
But Etan isn't using any Curse\nCrests... Hmm, it's so\nmysterious...
I feel like you're thinking about\nthis from the wrong angle...

No, different paths to a
solution aren't a waste. The
point is how one eventually
arrives there.
Ba... Bacchus...?
Miss Lymle. That voracious\nAcademic Thirst of yours is\ntruly wonderful.

I, Bacchus, am deeply
impressed. If it is acceptable
to you, I shall serve as a guide
to lead you to the answer.

Lymle, your curiosity is great,
but your attitude in facing
those questions is equally
worthy of praise.

Formulating and verifying
hypotheses is logical. Not
relying on others for answers
shows you have the
temperament of a scholar.

Ah, I believe Lymle's great
power as a mage comes not
just from her aptitude, but also
largely from her personality.

Miss Lilia, I suggest forming
hypotheses to address your
questions. If you wish, I shall
serve as your guide.
Hmph...
You look quite dissatisfied.
...C-could it be that I am not a\nsufficient guide?
Uncle Bacchus, you usually call\nLym-chan "Lymle," so why do\nyou call me "Miss Lilia"?
T-that is...
No, that's not it!
Not it...? Do you mean to say\nyou have already reached the\nanswer on your own?
Honestly, Lim doesn't know\nanything about being a "Miss"! I\nam Lymle!
I'm not Miss Lilia either, just\nRelia. I want you to call me\nRelia.
No, but, Miss Lilia... I believe\ncalling you by your first name\nwould be quite rude.

My teacher on Earth said that
remembering names and calling
each other by them is the first
step to becoming friends.
I know the true meaning behind\nthose words.
When we first met, Fidel and\nMiki called my name so many\ntimes.

It made me so happy. By
calling my name, the two of
them gave me a place where I
belong.

But the way you address me,
Uncle Bacchus, is a little
lonely... It makes me feel like
you're far away.
...No, I didn't mean it that way...

I want to become even closer
to you, Uncle Bacchus, during
our journey ahead. I want to
talk about so many things.
So, please, just call me Relia!

Hmm, a well-reasoned
argument, incorporating both
personal experience and
knowledge.

Bacchus. It seems Relia
possesses logical thinking skills
without you even needing to
teach her.

Miss Reli... no, Relia. Your
argument is perfectly valid.
Very well. I shall call you Relia
from now on.
Yeah, thank you!
Now, let's get back to the\nsubject at hand. Regarding the\nmechanism of the Replicate...
I think we should save that\ndiscussion for when we return\nto the ship.
More importantly, exploring\nthese ruins takes precedence.

Ruins that reflect human
memories... It likely accesses
and recreates the brains of
those within, specifically the
cerebral cortex.
Does that mean these ruins\ncan peek inside my head!?

That isn't difficult technology.
Analyzing brain signals to read
emotions or visualize images
has existed for hundreds of
years.

However, Miss Fayt mentioned
that events she had no
memory of were being
replayed.

You mean the story where
Grandpa Adray told Fayt he
really wanted Clair to be his
bride?
But Fayt, Grandpa Adray, and\nClair all said they have no\nmemory of that at all.

That is an intriguing
phenomenon. If that is the
case, then what is being read
is a desire...

True, it is hard to believe that
something without a clear form,
like a desire, could coalesce
into such a vivid reality.
If that is so, then the only\nthing left to consider is...
So this is that logical thinking\nUncle Bacchus was talking\nabout.
It is a vital way of thinking for\nthose facing the unknown,\nmuch like Mista Ernest.

...Could we hypothesize that
these ruins are extracting
information directly from our
brains...?

...If I recall, there was a lecture
at the University of
Princebridge on the causal
determination of uncertain
variables.

I can't exactly go back and
attend lectures in Energy
Nede, but it might be worth
searching for similar literature...
Hm!
Yo, Claude. What brings you to\nthis sacred hall of learning?
Oh, it's nothing important,\nreally...

Well, it's good that you came
nonetheless. There is an
infinite amount of knowledge
here for us to learn.
Everyone seems to be listening\nto the lectures quite quietly.
That's because it's currently\nexam season.

Is this... a memory of watching
a lecture at the university in
Princebridge, back in Energy
Nede...?
So Mista Ernest and the others\nhad visited Energy Nede\nbefore.
I see, so for you Morphus, they\nwere former comrades who\nwent their separate ways.
Yeah, seeing them study so\ndesperately reminds me of my\nstudent days in EnII... Hmm?

Everyone seems to be writing
things on small scraps of
paper instead of notebooks. I
wonder what they're doing?

That's called cheating. They
take out those little papers
during the exam to copy the
answers onto their sheets.
What?! Are they allowed to do\nthat?!
Of course not!! Mista Ernest,\nwhat kind of things are you\nteaching a young child!!

An exam is meant to show the
results of your daily studies. If
you listened to lectures
seriously, you wouldn't need
such things.
Seriously, huh? A safe\nanswer, but it lacks any spark.
Wh-what?!
Listen. An exam is a serious\nbattle between the examiner\nand the student.
The student tries to cheat\nwithout being caught, and the\nexaminer tries to catch them.
It's a battle where both sides\npour their heart and soul into\nit.
*Sigh*...
Bacchus, you use that body of\nyours to look things up all the\ntime, don't you?
I do, but... what does that have\nto do with what you're saying!?

There's no need to memorize
knowledge. You just need to
look it up when the time
comes.
Just like you do, Bacchus.
That is a completely different\nmatter from an exam! In the\nfirst place, an exam is...!
Um, it's like this, right?

Even if you try to remember
everything from class, it's hard
to be perfect. The teacher said
we should take notes to read
them again.

But even if it's in your
notebook, if you forget what
the class was about, you won't
know where to start reading.

I bet it's really hard to
remember everything on
planets like Earth that have all
sorts of amazing technology.

But if you remember the exam
topics, you can look them up
whenever you want to learn
more!
So, you're saying it's necessary\nto take exams seriously?

Yeah. Because if you hadn't
been listening seriously to the
lectures in Energy Nede, Uncle
Ernest...

You wouldn't have remembered
the lecture that might lead to
solving the mysteries of these
ruins, right?

Knowledge to research
knowledge, and knowledge to
connect it. Lectures and
exams exist solely to acquire
them.
Maybe they use tiny scraps of\npaper so they can easily pull\nthem out and reread them.

...To think I'd be outwitted by a
mere child. This is a fascinating
experience. I've learned
something today.

This story has ended. We plan
to release various other stories
in the future. Please look
forward to them.
